First Light

Now

Updated 2026 · 06 · 12  ·  Truchas, New Mexico

A short note about what I am doing right now, in case you are curious or in case you wrote to ask. I try to update this page every two or three months.

In the shop

I am about three weeks into a commission for a client in Abiquiú — a long sideboard in quartersawn white oak, with hand-cut dovetails on the case and through-tenoned legs. The wood is from a small mill near Pecos that I have been buying from for four years. The drawing went through six revisions before I started cutting. I expect to deliver it in late August. After that I have nothing on the calendar until October, on purpose.

Outside

The orchard is in its third year and the early apples are setting fruit for the first time. I am thinning, which is the hardest part of growing apples for me because it feels, the whole time, like vandalism. The ditch is running well this season. The fence at the south end is, as always, complaining.

Reading

I am most of the way through Paul Horgan's Great River, a long history of the Rio Grande that I started in January and keep returning to in the evenings. Alongside it, slowly, The Soul of a Tree by George Nakashima, which I read three or four pages of at a time and never tire of. On the kitchen table right now is a thin volume of Jane Kenyon, which my wife brought home from the library last week and which I have started underlining, lightly, in pencil.

Listening

Mostly the wind, the dog, and a small AM radio in the shop that picks up a Spanish-language station out of Las Vegas, NM, which plays cumbias on Saturday afternoons. In the truck I have been listening to old recordings of Doc Watson and almost nothing else.

What is going well

The writing is finding its pace again after a long slow spell in the spring. I sent the May essay on time, which I had not managed since November, and the June one is roughed out and not embarrassing. The shop is clean. The roof, which I worried about all winter, held.

What I am worried about

The fire season. The county had a bad one in 2022 and the conditions this June are not unlike that year — dry winter, early heat, wind from the wrong direction. I have spent more weekends than I would like clearing brush along the property line, and I am thinking about a metal-roof addition for the shop, which I cannot quite afford but cannot quite not afford either. I am also worried, in a smaller and more chronic way, about my mother in Albuquerque, who is well but slowing.

What I am saying no to

A few teaching invitations, a podcast, two requests to write for publications that pay well and that I respect. The reason in each case is the same: I do not have the time and if I had the time I would want to spend it in the shop. I am trying to be polite about it. I am not always succeeding.

What I am looking forward to

A trip to the high country in late July with two old friends, the first such trip in three years. Cooler nights. The first ripe peach off the young tree, which I think will happen sometime in August if the squirrels do not get there first. The essay I want to write in the fall about the long process of learning a place.

This page is in the spirit of the /now page movement, a quiet convention started by Derek Sivers.
